reasons: [coverage/major] D1 [criteriaAssessments C3; practicalImplications[0]; alternatives b1/b2; edgeCasesAndFailureModes] The capacity report covers the primary only ('prod-orders-pg, primary'), and E7 records 2 read replicas. A streaming physical replica holds the same data, so it fills at the same rate unless its volume is grown too. The draft's resize plan (verdict, C3, practicalImplications item 1, alternative b1) talks only about 'the volume'. It never says the two replica volumes, and any standby or backup target, must be grown first or at the same time. It also never says that a mass DELETE, pg_repack or partition export produces a WAL burst that has to fit on both the primary and the replicas. G3 in the packet asks about 'effects on replicas and backups', and the draft only touches this through the unresearched 'replica rebuild times'. A team that follows the plan as written could resize the primary and still lose a replica to a full disk.

[alternatives_counterarguments/major] D2 [alternatives b3; CL8; criteriaAssessments C2 mechanisms; tradeoffs[2]] Alternative b3 ('archive only, without a resize') is rejected because pg_repack needs about 480 GB free. That reasoning assumes the freed space has to be returned to the OS. audit_events is append-only (E5). The draft's own E12 says plain VACUUM keeps freed space for reuse within the same table. So exporting and then batch-DELETEing the old rows, with no rewrite at all, would let new audit inserts reuse roughly 780 GB inside the table. That stops audit_events from growing on disk for years and cuts net disk growth to only the non-audit tables, with no exclusive lock and no extra free space for a rewrite. The draft never weighs this cheaper option. It also never weighs the option's real risks: WAL volume from a 780 GB DELETE on a disk that is 92% full, vacuum load, and replica lag. Those risks, not the pg_repack space need, are what should drive the order of resize and archival. The fair comparison and the case for resizing first are therefore not properly argued.
D1 research part (replica volume layout) is internal infrastructure data not obtainable by web search
